summary: This schedule explains what a company whose shares are traded on a stock exchange must disclose when preparing and publishing its financial results. It covers rules for accounting policy changes, auditor modifications, new business names, uncommenced operations, exceptional items, and dividends. Companies must follow proper accounting standards and give clear details on any material events.
points: The listed entity must disclose any changes in accounting policies according to the applicable accounting standards.
The listed entity must disclose any modified opinions by the auditor and their cumulative impact on financial items.
The listed entity must disclose separate financial figures for a new line of business if it changes its name to suggest one.
The listed entity must disclose details of raised funds, project status, and expected commercial production dates if it has not commenced operations yet.
The listed entity must disclose all items of income and expenditure arising from transactions of an exceptional nature.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited changed its name to Meera Digital Services Private Limited to suggest a brand-new line of business. Because of this name change, the company must disclose the net sales, expenditure, and net profit or loss after tax figures pertaining specifically to this new digital business separately in its financial results. It must continue making these separate disclosures for the three years succeeding the date of the change in its name. Additionally, the company must correctly allocate its tax expenses between the new digital business and its other business based on the ratio of their respective net profits before tax.

terms.meaning: An auditor's report that is not entirely clean, showing a qualification, adverse view, or disclaimer regarding the financial statements.
Unusual items of income and expenditure arising out of transactions that need separate disclosure for clarity.
Proportionate division or distribution based on an exact share, amount, or time period.
A business that is assumed will continue operating into the foreseeable future without closing down.

watch: Make sure not to confuse unquantifiable audit impacts where estimates are mandatory with exceptions like going concerns where management may be permitted to omit estimates.
